digest.en: Central Asian migrants are struggling with Russia's new school rules, leading to family separations. In contrast, torrential rainfall in the Asia-Pacific region is causing widespread disruptions, with Japan's earthquake death toll rising as rescue efforts continue.
digest.hi: आज बोर्ड पर लीड स्टोरीज़: PoK की सड़कों पर कत्ल-ए-आम, फौज ने 2 दिन में 40 को मारा, लाशें भी कर दीं गायब, भारत से मदद की गुहार। पाकिस्तान ने रावलाकोट की हिंसा पर घेराबंदी की, एमनेस्टी ने जांच करने को कहा। ईरान ने अमेरिकी ठिकानों पर सरप्राइज अटैक किया, होर्मुज पर संग्राम हुआ।

articles.title: For Central Asian Migrants, Russia's School Rules Are Splitting Families
articles.summary: As the new school year approaches, Central Asian migrant parents face a stark choice: bring their children to Russia and risk them being unable to enroll because of stricter Russian language rules or leave them behind. For Central Asian Migrants, Russia's School Rules Are Splitting Families.

articles.title: Is torrential rainfall our new normal?
articles.summary: This week on Tipping Point, we dive into the climate chaos unfolding across continents. In India, torrential rains have paralyzed life in Mumbai and much of Maharashtra, leaving at least 15 dead and crippling transport systems. Neighbouring Pakistan is reeling under similar monsoon fury. Meanwhile, on the other side of the globe, Europe battles a different extreme. raging wildfires ignited by relen.

articles.title: A380 flight to China becomes 10-hour ordeal
articles.summary: It was a rare sight of an Emirates Airbus A380 - the world’s largest passenger airliner - at Hangzhou. But the situation soon became chaotic as 373 passengers were left stranded on board amid a logistical nightmare. A380 flight to China becomes 10-hour ordeal.

articles.title: Japan earthquake death toll rises as rescue teams search for missing
articles.summary: Military mobilises thousands of personnel after quake on southern Kyushu island that registered a maximum 7 on the Japanese shindo intensity scale At least five people have been killed, and nine are missing after a 6.8 magnitude earthquake struck southern Japan on Tuesday, injuring hundreds and knocking out power and water to tens of thousands. Military mobilises thousands of personnel after quake on southern Kyushu island that registered a maximum 7 on the Japanese shindo intensity scale At least 13 people were killed when a 6.8 magnitude earthquake struck southern Japan on Tuesday, injuring hundreds and knocking out power and water to tens of thousands.“There are people who are still waiting to be rescued, and it’s a race against time,.

articles.title: Remember the two-state solution? Trump doesn’t
articles.summary: Israel’s right-wing government is intensifying its half-century-long campaign to take over the West Bank fully by unleashing bands of settler militias to harass Palestinian residents, destroy their homes and livelihoods and restrict their movement throughout the occupied territory. The aim is to quickly erase conditions necessary for creating a viable Palestinian state alongside Israel, a [] The Remember the two-state solution?

articles.title: Bank Indonesia drama shows why rupiah is plunging
articles.summary: TOKYO. Investors hoping President Prabowo Subianto might learn from Indonesia’s past economic mistakes should get used to disappointment. Since taking office in October 2024, Prabowo has worked to drag Southeast Asia’s biggest economy back into its past. Which past is debatable. What isn’t debatable: the general-turned-politician is overseeing Indonesia’s worst financial turmoil since the [] The Bank Indonesia drama shows why rupiah is plunging.

articles.title: FCC bans humanoid robots from China, citing ‘unacceptable risks’
articles.summary: Move comes as the Trump administration has increasingly sought to keep Chinese technology out of the USThe Federal Communications Commission announced a ban on humanoid robots from China on Tuesday, saying that the technology poses “unacceptable risks” to the country’s national security. The move comes as the Trump administration has increasingly sought to keep Chinese technology out of the US.

articles.title: Russia Sanctions Bill Shows 'Bipartisan Coalition Of Support' For Ukraine
articles.summary: Ahead of a Senate vote on a sanctions package targeting Russia and Iran, Democratic Senator Sheldon Whitehouse, a co-sponsor of the legislation, told RFE/RL that the legislation sends a strong message that the United States is committed to supporting Ukraine. Russia Sanctions Bill Shows 'Bipartisan Coalition Of Support' For Ukraine.

articles.title: Russia-Iran Sanctions Bill Signals Congress United Behind Ukraine, Senator Whitehouse Tells RFE/RL
articles.summary: As the US Senate prepared to vote on a sweeping bipartisan sanctions package targeting Russia and Iran, Democratic Senator Sheldon Whitehouse, a co-sponsor of the legislation, said the measure reflects renewed bipartisan resolve to squeeze the Kremlin war machine and reinforce support for Ukraine. Russia-Iran Sanctions Bill Signals Congress United Behind Ukraine, Senator Whitehouse Tells RFE/RL.

articles.title: Ukraine Hits At Iran. In The Caspian Sea, Things Get Even Messier.
articles.summary: Russia’s Iranian-designed drones have ravaged Ukrainian forces in Moscow’s all-out war. As far as Ukraine is concerned, that means cargo ships plying the Caspian Sea with Iranian military goods are fair game. Including this past weekend. Ukraine Hits At Iran In The Caspian Sea. And Things Get Even Messier. In The Caspian Sea, Things Get Even Messier.

articles.title: Mount Olympus and D-Day beaches among new World Heritage Sites
articles.summary: From the peaks of Mount Olympus in Greece to the shores of the “D-Day” beaches in France, 25 cultural or natural landmarks from across the globe have been newly inscribed on the World Heritage List, updated annually by the UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). Mount Olympus and D-Day beaches among new World Heritage Sites.

articles.title: HIV, hepatitis, STI gains at risk as funding falls, WHO warns
articles.summary: Years of progress in tackling HIV, viral hepatitis and sexually transmitted infections (STIs) are at risk of stalling, leaving millions of people without access to life-saving prevention, testing and treatment, the World Health Organization (WHO) has warned. HIV, hepatitis, STI gains at risk as funding falls, WHO warns.

articles.title: IOM warns trafficking networks are booming
articles.summary: A job advert can hide a criminal network, and a single click can lead to a nightmare. Hundreds of thousands of people are trafficked every year on the promise of legitimate work abroad, only to be held captive and forced into online scam operations. IOM warns trafficking networks are booming.

articles.title: Updates on Gaza, West Bank amid regional tensions
articles.summary: Regional tensions are mounting as the US-Iran war continues and a rising number of Israeli attacks are threatening Gaza’s fragile October ceasefire that ended two years of war with Hamas. Security Council members are hearing updates on Tuesday. Join our live coverage. Updates on Gaza, West Bank amid regional tensions. Security Council members heard briefings followed by an open debate on Tuesday.

articles.title: Javier Milei accuses US Democrats of financing ‘anti-Argentina campaign’ at World Cup
articles.summary: President also blames Brazil and Mexico and says online critics ‘do not want the ideas of freedom to succeed’More than a week has passed since Ferran Torres scored the extra-time goal that gave Spain its second World Cup, but – at least for Argentina’s president – the tournament is not over. Javier Milei accuses US Democrats of financing ‘anti-Argentina campaign’ at World Cup.

articles.title: Canada’s GCAP fighter move tests limits of US diversification
articles.summary: Canada’s entry into the Global Combat Air Program (GCAP) highlights a broader strategic dilemma: how to modernize its air force without deepening dependence on any single supplier or undermining the interoperability on which its defense commitments rely. This month, multiple media outlets reported that Canada officially joined the GCAP as its first observer nation, marking [] The post Canada’s GC.

articles.title: Zelenskyy, Trump Meet At White House At Crucial Moment In US-Ukraine Relations
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had "a good meeting" with US President Donald Trump on July 28. The meeting, which had been expected to be one of the most consequential moments in US-Ukraine relations since Donald Trump's return to the White House, lasted about a hour. Zelenskky, Trump Meet At White House At Crucial Moment In US-Ukraine Relations. Zelenskyy, Trump Meet At White House At Crucial Moment In US-Ukraine Relations.

articles.title: Vietnam’s smart-port push opens another door to Washington
articles.summary: Vietnam’s effort to modernize Da Nang’s maritime infrastructure may look at first like another Asian port-development project, but it is considerably more important than that. The transformation underway along Vietnam’s central coast brings together three priorities that increasingly define Hanoi’s foreign policy: economic modernization, technological self-reliance and stronger maritime awareness Vietnam’s smart-port push opens another door to Washington.

articles.title: Iran War Drives Central Asian Countries To Seek Alternate Trade Routes
articles.summary: In an interview with RFE/RL, Ken Moriyasu, a senior fellow at the Hudson Institute, said the countries of Central Asia appear to be giving up on Iran as a gateway to global trade, a situation which is driving new approaches to cooperation with China and Pakistan. Iran War Drives Central Asian Countries To Seek Alternate Trade Routes.

articles.title: Central Asia Is Increasingly Looking Beyond Iran, Says Analyst Ken Moriyasu
articles.summary: Has the Iran conflict permanently reshaped Central Asia's strategic map? Hudson Institute senior fellow Ken Moriyasu explains why governments across the region are increasingly looking beyond Iran toward Pakistan, Afghanistan and China for trade, connectivity, and access to global markets. Central Asia Is Increasingly Looking Beyond Iran, Says Analyst Ken Moriyasu.

articles.title: Pinochet-era soldier jailed for killing folk singer Víctor Jara 53 years ago
articles.summary: Nelson Haase Mazzei was sentenced for murdering Víctor Jara in 2023, but fled from authorities in ChileMore than 50 years after the murder of the Chilean folk singer Víctor Jara, the last man wanted in connection with his death has been tracked down and brought to justice. Nelson Haase Mazzei was sentenced for murdering Jara in 2023, but fled from authorities in ChileMore than 50 years after the murder of the Chilean folk singer Víctor Jara, the last man wanted in connection with his death has been tracked down and brought to justice. Nelson Haase Mazzei, a retired colonel, fled from authorities in 2023 after he and six other retired soldiers were sentenced in absent.

articles.title: 60-Year-Old Ukrainian Volunteer Supplies Front Lines Amid Rise Of Unmanned Ground Vehicles
articles.summary: Russian drone attacks are making it increasingly dangerous to deliver supplies to Ukraine's frontline troops. While Kyiv is deploying unmanned ground vehicles for some risky missions, volunteers like 60-year-old Mykhaylo continue making supply runs the old-fashioned way in the Donetsk region. 60-Year-Old Ukrainian Volunteer Supplies Front Lines Amid Rise Of Unmanned Ground Vehicles.

articles.title: 75 years later, the promise to protect refugees faces its greatest test
articles.summary: As the world marks the 75th anniversary of the Refugee Convention, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) has launched a global campaign urging governments, organizations and individuals to renew their commitment to protecting people forced to flee war, violence and persecution. 75 years later, the promise to protect refugees faces its greatest test.

articles.title: High prices and funding cuts stall HIV prevention revolution
articles.summary: The AIDS epidemic could stage a comeback amid unequal access to breakthrough prevention medicines and a sharp decline in global funding, according to a UN report released on Monday ahead of the opening of the 26th International AIDS Conference in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. High prices and funding cuts stall HIV prevention revolution.

articles.summary: जापान हर रोज चार बार भूकंप के झटके झेलता है और फिर भी तरक्की करता है। Japan Earthquake Story: हर बार सब कुछ तबाह होने के बाद जापान दोगुने जोश के साथ खड़ा हो जाता है और दुनिया को पीछे छोड़ते हुए तरक्की की नई इबारत लिख देता है. यह सोच 1945 में दूसरे विश्वयुद्ध में परमाणु बम हमले से लेकर रोजाना सुनामी और भूकंप जैसी घटनाओं तक में निपटने के काम में आती है.
